description: Multi-head attention forward. Q is [batch, heads, seqlen_q, head_dim]; K and V share seqlen_k.

heads_kv.description: KV head count. Equal to heads is MHA, 1 is MQA, anything between is GQA.

head_dim.description: Per-head width. 8 and up: narrower is not an attention head, and without a range the search spends half its draws below 16.

value_head_dim.description: Width of V, and so of O (and dO, dV), against Q and K's head_dim. same (default): equal, as nearly every model has. mla: 64 narrower, DeepSeek's multi-head latent attention, whose Q and K carry a 64-wide rotary part that V does not -- 192/128 in prefill and training, 576/512 with the latent absorbed in decode. hipDNN requires only Q and K's last dims to agree (SdpaFwdNode Rule 2, SdpaBwdNode Rule 3; O, dO and dV take V's), and ASM SDPA and FlyDSL ship kernels for such pairs. Declared only with head_dim >= 128, so V keeps 64 or more.

alignment.description: Which corner the diagonal is anchored at. Only a distinct problem where the mask is causal or windowed and seqlen_q < seqlen_k; the constraint below pins it to top_left everywhere else, so the sweep does not spend half its budget measuring each shape twice. An engine that serves one anchor and refuses the other is removed from a comparison by the corpus rather than by a measurement, which is why this is a declared axis rather than a fixed choice.

dtype.description: Element type of Q, K and V. fp16, bf16 and fp32 write O in the same type. The four fp8 encodings are graphs with the three per-tensor Q, K and V descales every fp8 plan requires, and with O (and the bias, under the bias form) in bf16, which is what the fp8 plans write; the "// types" note under graph_builder has the matrix and where each rule comes from. fp8_e4m3_fnuz is the encoding gfx942 hardware and the shipped ASM kernels use, so it holds twice the weight of the other three. OCP fp8_e4m3 and the two e5m2 encodings are valid hipDNN graphs that the references run and every shipped engine declines; they are declared so a model is not first shown an fp8 type at inference. The weights hold fp8 to about a sixth of the sweep and each of the other three types to about 28%, where each had a third before fp8 was declared. Weighted, dtype splits the first pass's budget rather than multiplying it, as layout, scale, window and value_head_dim do.

generate_stats.description: The training forward: also write the softmax statistics (logsumexp) the backward pass consumes.

layout.description: Memory order of the attention operands; dims stay (B, H, S, D) and the order lives in the strides. bshd (default) is token-major for every tensor, [S*H*D, D, H*D, 1]. bhsd is head-major for every tensor, [H*S*D, S*D, D, 1]. kv_bhsd is the decode KV cache: Q, O (and dO, dQ) token-major and K, V (and dK, dV) head-major. Statistics stay row-major. Which layouts an engine serves differs a great deal, so this is a declared axis and the engine oracle filters it; it is not part of the regime label. Extents of 1 make layouts alias (with seqlen_q 1 and heads 1, kv_bhsd is bhsd; with seqlen_k 1 and heads_kv 1, it is bshd), so the constraints below leave kv_bhsd out of those points: the same graph would otherwise be listed under two layouts. sbhd is sequence-major, Megatron's [S, B, H, D]: [H*D, D, B*H*D, 1] for every tensor; with one batch, or one row in both sequences, it is bshd, so it is declared only where batch > 1 and a sequence is longer than 1. qkv_packed: Q, K and V (and dQ, dK, dV) are views of one fused QKV projection, a row of heads*head_dim + heads_kv*head_dim + heads_kv*value width per token, so each has [S*R, W, R, 1] for its own width W; O and dO stay token-major. A fused QKV projection is self-attention, so qkv_packed is declared only with seqlen_q == seqlen_k. The ragged form packs tokens through offset tensors and needs token-major strides, so it is declared only with the token-major bshd and qkv_packed.

scale.description: The attention scale. inv_sqrt_d (default) is 1/sqrt(head_dim). unit is 1.0, a model that folds the scale into Q. jitter is 1/sqrt(head_dim) times (0.5 + 0.15 * r) for r = (seqlen_k + 3*seqlen_q + batch + head_dim) % 13, a deterministic stand-in for an arbitrary scale in [0.5, 2.3] times the standard one. The modulus is 13 so that power-of-two extents, which fill the archetypes, spread over 12 of the 13 residues instead of landing on one, and no residue gives exactly 1 (so jitter is never the inv_sqrt_d graph). Never 0: a zero scale means unset and omits the attribute. It is the stated value only where the form states one: scale_unset states none and scale_tensor passes it as a runtime tensor, so those two take inv_sqrt_d (the constraints below), and one graph is not listed under three scales.

window.description: Sliding window: local_N keeps the N keys ending at the diagonal (left bound N; the right bound is whatever the mask sets, 0 under a causal mask). none (default) has no left bound. The left bound is never 0, which the frontend rejects. The frontend accepts a left bound under any mask, so the window is not tied to a causal mask here; an engine that serves windows only causally is filtered by the oracle. A window with seqlen_q > seqlen_k is excluded: with the diagonal anchored top-left, every query row from seqlen_k + N - 1 on would keep no key at all.

form.description: Which optional attributes and tensors the graph binds (RFC 0019 §6.7, absent is not zero, and §6.8 rule 9: a model must tolerate any optional feature a valid graph leaves unbound). One aspect varies per graph from the plain baseline, so every optional input appears both present and absent without crossing them all. plain states the scale and binds nothing optional; scale_unset leaves the scale unstated; scale_tensor gives it as a pass-by-value tensor; dropout adds Philox dropout with an INT64 seed and offset; padded adds per-batch seq_len_q and seq_len_kv; ragged packs Q, O and the statistics through one offset tensor and K and V through another (compact THD, no length tensors); bias adds an additive [1, 1, seqlen_q, seqlen_k] bias; sink adds one FLOAT sink logit per query head. A --model-shapes file with no `q.form` column reads every row as plain; a column left empty in a row is refused. Every form is an even stratum, and the forms are not weighted (unlike layout, scale and window), so the cut to --count takes each form evenly, as far as the first pass holds it. Without --count the forms declared in fewer combinations get fewer graphs: scale_unset and scale_tensor take inv_sqrt_d only and ragged takes the token-major layouts (bshd, qkv_packed) only. --form-floor tops each form up to its count. Interactions: the form decides whether the `scale` facet applies (scale_unset and scale_tensor ignore it, so they are held at inv_sqrt_d) and which `layout` is meaningful (ragged is token-major: bshd and qkv_packed only). Every other pairing with layout, window and scale is a valid graph; an engine that serves only some of them is filtered by the oracle.

// regime_label: The populations a corpus is reported per, as RFC 0019.13 §11.2's regret table needs them.
Phase: decode is one query token against a cache and is memory bound on that cache;
prefill is the whole prompt at once and is compute bound on the score matrix. They are the
same operation and entirely different problems, which is why they are anchored as separate
archetypes rather than as one range over seqlen_q. Cross attention (more queries than keys)
draws its two sequences from different tensors, so it varies independently of the rest --
the constraint admits it only under a non-causal mask, and the clause files it under
Grouping (mha/gqa/mqa) is the third facet: how many query heads share one KV head decides
how much of the KV cache a wavefront re-reads, which is the whole difference between a
decode that is bandwidth bound and one that is not. It is a label rather than a bucket
because what matters is heads_kv relative to heads, not its magnitude.
// form_label: The optional aspects a graph binds, reported as a facet column of its own and counted by --form-floor.
Not part of the regime label above: forms cross every regime, so joining them in would multiply
the regime names (and break the quotas keyed on them) instead of adding a column.
Each non-plain value is one clause on the declared `form` parameter, so a focused search pins it.
// kernel_catalog: How a descriptor pack's metadata reads back as a point. The pack names its fields whatever
the kernel author named them; this is the only place those spellings appear, so a new pack
vocabulary is a declaration edit rather than a code change. A descriptor missing any mapped
field carries no geometry and contributes nothing -- which is how pointwise_add and the
shipped tiled_attention are excluded without naming them anywhere.
A pack value with no entry under `enums` is skipped and counted, never guessed: a pack in
fp8 read as bf16 would produce a corpus of graphs the engine does not serve, labelled as
`constants` answers for a parameter the pack vocabulary has no field for at all. These
packs record `causal` without recording which corner the diagonal is anchored at, because
every kernel in them anchors it top-left; saying so here is what lets the builder resolve
an argument no descriptor supplies. A parameter mapped under `metadata` is refused here,
so a constant can never overwrite what a descriptor actually said.
// model_shape_defaults: A model-shape CSV written before one of these parameters was declared has no column for it; the file's rows then mean the default named here. Only these: a parameter with no column and no entry here (alignment, generate_stats, ...) is refused, since filling it in would pass off an unrecorded shape as recorded. The pack `constants` above answer for kernel packs and are not used for shape files.

// types: Operands carry the declared dtype; accumulation and the score matrix are fp32. Left to default, compute follows io and every fp16/bf16 graph is uniform half precision, which hip-kernel-provider's SdpaFwdPlanBuilder and SdpaBwdPlanBuilder refuse outright ('compute_data_type must be FLOAT') and the ingestor engines decline at graph_match -- a live-engine corpus then admits nothing, indistinguishable from naming an engine that does not exist. The training forward's softmax statistics are fp32.

The dtype matrix, one row per `dtype`: the types of Q, K, V and O, and the operands the graph carries beyond those the `form` adds. Every row has compute type FLOAT and leaves mma_core_mode unset, which every engine accepts (FlyDSL and rocKE take UNSET, HALF or BFLOAT16 on 16-bit graphs, FlyDSL UNSET or FLOAT on fp32, ASM UNSET, HALF or BFLOAT16 on bf16 and UNSET, FP8_E4M3 or FP8_E5M2 on fp8; no combination needs a value), so mma_core_mode is not an axis here.

fp16, bf16, fp32: Q, K, V and O alike; no further operand. hipDNN's references register all three (SdpaFwdSignatureKey::getPlanBuilders). The ingestor engines require one type across Q, K, V and O (flydsl_sdpa_cdna, rocKE's UnifiedAttentionGraphMatch), so the mixed graph the references also take, fp16 or bf16 in and fp32 out, is not declared.

fp8_e4m3, fp8_e5m2, fp8_e4m3_fnuz, fp8_e5m2_fnuz: Q, K and V in that encoding, O in bf16, and Descale_Q, Descale_K and Descale_V, each FLOAT, one element ([1, 1, 1, 1]), an ordinary device tensor rather than a pass-by-value one. Each part is a rule of a plan or of the references. The three descales are required for an fp8 input and rejected for any other (isSupportedSdpaFwdNode; SdpaFwdPlanBuilder.cpp checkFp8Descales for ASM). ASM reads them through a device pointer and so refuses a pass-by-value or virtual one (checkDeviceTensor); the references take either, and an ordinary tensor is the one both take. ASM needs one element per descale (isScalarTensor: 'per-tensor scalars'); the references' per-KV-head [B, H_kv, 1, 1] descale is not declared. O is bf16 because ASM writes nothing else for fp8 (getDataTypeIdentifier) and the references take it, as they take an fp8 O in the input's encoding, which needs scale_o and amax_o that no engine here implements. hipDNN's frontend checks no Q, K, V or O type (SdpaFwdNode::pre_validate_node) and its backend only that the node's compute type is set (SdpaFwdOperationDescriptor::finalize): the descales and the bf16 O are what the plans that take fp8 require, and a graph without them is valid and run by none.

The bias, under the bias form, takes Q's dtype for fp16, bf16 and fp32 and bf16 for fp8: the references take a mask in FLOAT, HALF or BFLOAT16 only (addPlanBuilderAllMasks), and FlyDSL a bias in Q's type or FLOAT. The rest of the operands keep their own types in every row: statistics FLOAT, the scale tensor FLOAT, the sink FLOAT, the lengths and offsets INT32, the dropout seed and offset INT64.

Not declared on any row: the softmax and output scaling of cuDNN's sdpa_fp8 (Descale_S, Scale_S, Scale_O, Amax_S, Amax_O). ASM declines each (SdpaFwdPlanBuilder.cpp checkFwdUnsupportedFeatures), FlyDSL and rocKE decline any fp8 scaling tensor (FlydslSdpaCdnaCommon, UnifiedAttentionGraphMatch), and only the references implement them (SEM-024 of SdpaSemanticsRegister.md).

Who serves what: fp8_e4m3_fnuz on gfx942 is the only fp8 row a shipped engine answers (ASM; it declines OCP fp8_e4m3 with 'gfx942 fp8 SDPA requires FP8_E4M3_FNUZ inputs' and takes no e5m2 input, getDataTypeIdentifier), FlyDSL and rocKE serve none, and ASM's forward kernels are bf16 only among the 16-bit rows. The live-engine oracle drops the rows an engine refuses, as it drops forms; the declaration does not.
graph_builder.// layout: BSHD (the default): dims stay (B, H, S, D) and the layout lives in the strides, token-major, as the shipped bundles lay them out. Not row-major: strides_of would give BHSD, and rocKE's dense kernels take no stride kernargs -- stride_q_tok is baked as Hq*D -- so their matcher (hasBshdStrides) declines every BHSD graph. AITER serves BSHD too, so the default keeps both engines in the contest. The `layout` parameter adds bhsd (head-major, [H*S*D, S*D, D, 1]) and kv_bhsd (Q/O token-major, K/V head-major, the decode KV cache), whose batch stride is BSHD's, so only the head and sequence strides differ; sbhd (Megatron's sequence-major order, batch stride H*D) and qkv_packed (Q, K and V as views of one fused QKV projection row, O token-major). value_head_dim mla narrows V, O (and dO, dV) by 64, so their strides use the value width wherever Q's use head_dim. An engine that serves only some of them is filtered by the oracle, per combination, not by a measurement. The ragged form packs tokens through offset tensors whose multiplier is the token stride, so it needs token-major strides and is declared only with bshd and qkv_packed; bhsd, kv_bhsd and sbhd with ragged would address data that is not token-contiguous per sequence through a token-packed container.
graph_builder.// scale: attnScale is the plain form's stated scale, not left to the schema's optional: rocKE's dense matcher declines a graph with no attn_scale_value (the scale is a required f32 kernarg and guessing 1/sqrt(D) is what it refuses to do), so a corpus that was all scale_unset would empty a rocKE corpus. 1/sqrt(head_dim) is the standard scale and what the shipped bundles carry. The other forms leave it out (scale_unset, scale_tensor) or keep it (the rest), and the live-engine oracle drops the forms an engine refuses, which is how rocKE's corpus stays free of them. The `scale` parameter chooses the stated value for the forms that state one; scale_unset states none and scale_tensor passes the value as a runtime tensor, so a constraint holds the facet at inv_sqrt_d there instead of listing the same graph (or tensors differing only in their default) under three scales. leftBound is declared only for a windowed problem; elsewhere the argument resolves to nothing and the builder leaves the bound unset.
graph_builder.// form: One optional aspect per graph, everything else as the plain graph has it. The conventions are hipDNN's own: seq_len_q and seq_len_kv are INT32 [B, 1, 1, 1] (SdpaFwdNode::validateSeqLenTensor); the offset tensors of a ragged operand are INT32 [B+1, 1, 1, 1] (detail::validateIndexTensor; SdpaVllmFormTestGraphs.hpp makeVllmGraph); the sink is one FLOAT logit per query head, [1, Hq, 1, 1] (validateSinkToken); the scale tensor is a single-element pass-by-value tensor (validateScalarParameter), given as a runtime parameter whose default is the plain form's scale; the bias takes Q's dtype (bf16 under fp8, see the types note) and dims [1, 1, seqlen_q, seqlen_k], row-major (the node's ATTN_MASK rule: last two dims equal seq_q and seq_kv, or 1). The dropout seed and offset are INT64 [1, 1, 1, 1] device tensors as the test SDK builds them (RaggedSdpaDensifyTestGraphs.hpp withPhiloxDropout); the frontend states no rule for them, so that one is the test SDK's convention, not a validated one. ragged is makeVllmGraph's compact THD form with a ragged query and KV: Q and O share one offset tensor with multiplier heads*head_dim, the statistics the same tensor with multiplier heads (so ragged statistics are token-major, [seqlen_q*heads, 1, heads, 1], as there), K and V another with multiplier heads_kv*head_dim; no length tensors and no padding mask; the dims stay the padded (B, H, max_len, D) ones. Each multiplier is the tensor's token stride, which the BSHD strides above make heads*head_dim. Facet interactions are constraints, not builder guards: `scale` is held at inv_sqrt_d under scale_unset and scale_tensor, and `ragged` is held to the token-major layouts (bshd, qkv_packed). Everything else crosses freely (padded, dropout, bias and sink with every window; padded and ragged with cross attention), since the frontend validators, the CPU and GPU references and the engine matchers state those as valid or as an engine-level decline, which the oracle filters.

Bidirectional, as such attention is; a causal mask over more queries than keys is declared too (top-left, where every query row keeps a key), reached by exploration

// archetypes: Recorded transformer configurations (RFC 0019.13 §12.3). Decode and prefill are the same operation and different problems -- seqlen_q of 1 against a long cache is memory bound, and a square prefill is compute bound -- so each is anchored separately rather than left to a range over seqlen_q.
// neighbourhood: head_dim moves among the widths shipped models use rather than scaling, since an interpolated 100 or 144 is not a configuration anyone ships. seqlen_k mirrors seqlen_q at ratios >= 1, the relation of decoder attention (prefill and append); more queries than keys comes from exploration and the cross attention archetype.
// mixture: Same shares as conv_fwd; see the note there.
